issues.legal_issue: When the existence or genuineness of an arbitration agreement is denied in an application seeking appointment of an arbitrator, the appointing court must decide that issue and cannot leave it to the arbitrator.
material_facts: The respondents sought appointment of an arbitrator based on a memorandum containing an arbitration clause.
The appellant denied signing or executing the memorandum, and alleged in response to the proceedings that it was forged and fabricated.
The High Court appointed an arbitrator and left the legality, validity, and genuineness of the memorandum and arbitration agreement for the arbitrator to decide.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was required to decide whether the memorandum was a valid and genuine agreement before deciding whether to appoint an arbitrator. Its direction leaving that question to the arbitrator was set aside, and the matter was remanded for the court to decide the question on its merits.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 11 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, the Chief Justice or designate must decide whether an arbitration agreement exists and whether the applicant is a party to it; this jurisdictional issue cannot be left to the arbitral tribunal. Where forgery or fabrication is alleged, it is appropriate for the appointing court to decide the issue. The Court applied SBP & Co. v. Patel Engineering Ltd. (2005) 8 SCC 618, National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Boghara Polyfab (P) Ltd. (2009) 1 SCC 267, and Bharat Rasiklal Ashra v. Gautam Rasiklal Ashra (2012) 2 SCC 144.

rule.if: arbitrator_appointment_proceeding and agreement_existence_denied and document_forgery_alleged and court_left_threshold_issue_to_arbitrator

predicates.arbitrator_appointment_proceeding: A party applied to a court to appoint an arbitrator.
predicates.agreement_existence_denied: The opposing party denied that it had entered into the alleged arbitration agreement.
predicates.document_forgery_alleged: The opposing party alleged that the document said to contain the agreement was forged or fabricated.
predicates.court_left_threshold_issue_to_arbitrator: The court directed the arbitrator, rather than deciding the issue itself, to determine whether the agreement existed or was genuine.

issues.definition: When an arbitrator-appointment proceeding involves a denial of the agreement and an allegation that its document was forged, and the court has left that threshold issue to the arbitrator, the appointing court must decide the agreement's existence and genuineness before appointment.

issues.legal_issue: A party's failure to respond to a notice proposing an arbitrator does not prevent it from contesting the existence or genuineness of the agreement in subsequent appropriate proceedings when it raises that denial there.
material_facts: The respondents sent the appellant a letter proposing an arbitrator, and the appellant did not respond to that letter.
In response to the respondents' injunction proceeding, the appellant denied signing or executing the memorandum and alleged that it was forged and fabricated.
The appellant again denied the existence of the memorandum in its response to the application seeking appointment of an arbitrator.
issues.conclusion: The appellant's failure to respond to the appointment notice did not bar its challenge; its denials in the subsequent proceedings were sufficient to raise the issue in a timely manner.
issues.legal_principle: A denial of execution and genuineness raised in appropriate proceedings is sufficient to join issue on the agreement's validity and genuineness, notwithstanding the party's earlier failure to answer a notice proposing an arbitrator. The Court rejected the contention that the challenge was raised too late.

predicates.arbitrator_appointment_proceeding: A party applied to a court to appoint an arbitrator.
predicates.no_reply_to_appointment_notice: The party did not respond to a notice proposing an arbitrator.
predicates.agreement_denied_in_subsequent_proceedin: The party denied signing or entering into the alleged agreement in its pleadings in subsequent appropriate proceedings.

issues.definition: When a party does not respond to an appointment notice but denies the agreement in subsequent appropriate proceedings, the party may still contest the agreement's existence and genuineness.
